recommendation: Keep the source fix. It closes the current-build gap caused by later datatype refactoring without reverting later Pharmacy WG example wording.
issue_request: FHIR-7549 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the Pharmacy WG. It asked to clean up dosage.method definitions because the old note that method is often pre-coordinated with route or form did not say whether method, route, site, or form should be duplicated; the accepted resolution required clearer text across MedicationAdministration, MedicationOrder, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement.
initial_application: SVN r6688, imported as git commit d0e67474395d30f30ce638f3645578f4c9a7cc39, applied the FHIR-7549 wording to old MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement dosage spreadsheets. Current MedicationAdministration.dosage.method still carries the clarified wording, but later dosage datatype refactoring left the active shared Dosage.method row with the older terse pre-coordination comment.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Dosage as an active datatype and the relevant medication resources as active. MedicationOrder has since become MedicationRequest, and current MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement dosage elements use DosageDetails/Dosage-family datatype source rather than old resource-specific dosage.method rows. FHIR-19913 later corrected Dosage.method examples to "inject, swallow, or chew" and is already represented on the combined branch, so that later wording was preserved.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/dosage.xml so active Dosage.method now explains that the method is often not populated when route or form pre-coordinate the method, while retaining the later FHIR-19913 examples. No MedicationAdministration edit was needed because its active resource-specific element already had the clarified FHIR-7549 guidance.
source_changes: source/datatypes/dosage.xml: updated the Dosage.method definition and comment to include the FHIR-7549 guidance about route/form pre-coordination and method population frequency while preserving the current examples.
